Landed 32c7b126 on main (single-developer mode, self-reported gate, LocallyObserved).

Gate: embedBench/test 93/93 with pinned MiniLM artifacts supplied, so the env-gated neural
court executed (SherlockRecallMappingSuite 7 total, 0 ignored); scalafmtCheckAll clean.
Mutation: corrupting the leaf text in Built.nodeTexts failed exactly the named bridge court
(1 failed / 7 total, siblings green); reverted.

Artifacts: HF revision 1110a243, sha256 verified against the catalog pins before first use
(model 6fd5d72f..., tokenizer be50c362...), and re-verified by OnnxSentenceEmbedder.open.

Batch (33 transcript files; 17 unique subjects, the sub-* files duplicate NN01-NN16 under a
second naming scheme): neural vs lexical on identical inputs, same nominator budget
(perLevel=8) and cost model. Mean per-subject source mass 0.104 -> 0.651; mean external mass
0.896 -> 0.349; external mass fell for 33/33 files. Spot check (NN01): "he wakes up" ->
"John immediately gets up from his bed" (part-a 53s); "he's at his desk with a gun" ->
"John walks toward his desk" (part-b 1121s); the glass-bottle unit -> the pill-bottle
close-up (part-a 216s).

Operational finding worth remembering: sbt in-process runMain cannot host the DJL tokenizer
twice (native lib binds one classloader), and sbt's background run threads still print
[success], so a 33-run batch died after run 1 with exit 0. Detected by counting output files,
not by the status. Forked runs (set embedBench / Compile / run / fork := true) with absolute
paths are the working shape.

What this does not establish: no human gold standard, so per-unit anchor correctness is
spot-checked, not measured; external mass ~0.35 remains (some of it is genuinely external
commentary); scene nodes embed label-only text and rarely win MAP, which is acceptable for
leaf-precision media coordinates but unexamined as a modelling choice.
